tagline: Global leader in animal health, dedicated to innovating and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets
hero_kpi_rationale: Elanco positions innovation as a strategic pillar with an active pipeline of new products (Bovaer, Zenrelia, Befrena) and a targeted restructuring to strengthen its R&D capabilities in the United States, making it a key driver of differentiated growth.

kpis.name: R&D Investments as a Percentage of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Share of research and development expenses in revenue.
kpis.description: In 2025, Elanco invested $368 million in R&D on revenue of $4.715 billion, representing 7.8% of revenue. Elanco states it is an industry leader in R&D in animal health, with a portfolio of 200 brands and an active pipeline of new products.
kpis.signal: Moderate investment rate in innovation, characteristic of leaders in animal health.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin in 2025 was 55.0% ($2.593B gross profit / $4.715B revenue). It is affected by generic competition (e.g., Seresto) and regulatory changes on antibiotics.
kpis.signal: Solid margin but significantly declining, likely due to competitive pressure from generics.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Significant impact from 2025 restructuring charges ($237M), including $155M in restructuring costs and $1.042B in goodwill impairment. Operating margin is negative at -4.8%.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline due to restructuring charges, goodwill impairment, and pricing pressure.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending for the acquisition or modernization of physical assets.
kpis.description: Capex of $276M in 2025 (vs $147M in 2024), primarily for the expansion of the monoclonal antibody manufacturing facility in Elwood, Kansas, and investments related to restructuring.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in Capex for monoclonal antibody manufacturing capacity expansion and restructuring-related investments.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: The 2025 restructuring targets a reduction of approximately 300 positions and the repositioning of around 300 others to low-cost regions or growth areas.
kpis.signal: Headcount reduction as part of a restructuring to improve margin.

kpis.name: Restructuring Charges
kpis.explanation: One-time costs related to organizational restructuring.
kpis.description: $155M in restructuring charges in 2025, including $116M in employee-related costs and $39M in asset impairments. The plan was approved in December 2025 to optimize global footprint and invest in innovation. Additional charges of $25-30M are expected in 2026.
kpis.signal: Significant charge in 2025, reflecting a major strategic transformation.

kpis.name: Innovation Revenue
kpis.explanation: Measures revenue generated by new products and services to assess the company's innovation capability.

kpis.name: Pet Health Revenue
kpis.explanation: Measures revenue generated from pet health products, indicating the commercial performance of this segment.

kpis.name: Farm Animal Revenue
kpis.explanation: Measures sales of products for farm animals. Shows whether this Elanco business line is growing.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue measures the money earned by Elanco from selling its animal health products. It is the key indicator of growth.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Measures core profitability by excluding financial and non-recurring items to better assess operational health.

kpis.name: Bovaer Launch
kpis.explanation: Launch of the innovative anti-methane product for dairy cattle.
kpis.description: Bovaer (3-NOP) received FDA approval in May 2024 and was launched in the United States in Q3 2024. Producers began using it in 2024. However, adoption has been slowed by the absence of government incentives due to federal policy changes in 2025.
kpis.signal: Pioneering product in livestock sustainability. Bovaer launched in the U.S. in Q3 2024, but adoption slowed by the freeze in government incentives in 2025.

kpis.name: Antibiotics Revenue Mix
kpis.explanation: Share of sales related to antibiotics in total revenue.
kpis.description: In 2025, 9% of revenue came from shared (medically important) antibiotics and 15% from animal-specific antibiotics. Ionophores represent 89% of animal antibiotic revenue. Growing regulatory risks: EU restriction 2022, Vietnam ban January 2026.
kpis.signal: Significant regulatory exposure: 24% of revenue linked to antibiotics, with increasing risks of regulatory restrictions.

kpis.name: New Product Approvals
kpis.explanation: Number of regulatory approvals for new products in 2024-2025.
kpis.description: Bovaer (May 2024), Zenrelia (September 2024), Credelio Quattro (October 2024), AdTab (April 2025), Befrena (December 2025). These approvals demonstrate strong innovation capability in animal health.
kpis.signal: Active innovation pipeline with 5 major product approvals in 2024-2025.

risks.title: Substantial Indebtedness
risks.summary: The company has significant debt which could impact its ability to invest and grow, although the debt restructuring in 2025 improved the maturity profile.
risks.score_rationale: The company has substantial debt. In 2025, it refinanced $2.102B of Term Loan B with three new debt facilities (EUR 400M, $1.100B and $540M) maturing in 2029-2032. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Foreign Exchange Rate Fluctuations
risks.summary: Fluctuations in exchange rates could negatively impact the results of the company operating globally.
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in over 90 countries and is exposed to foreign exchange rate risks, which could impact its operating results. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Increasing Generic Competition
risks.summary: Patent expirations and the entry of generics will force the company to reduce prices and offer discounts, significantly impacting margins.
risks.score_rationale: The company faces growing competition from generic products. In January 2026, a competitor began selling a generic alternative to Seresto more than a year before patent expiration. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Regulatory Risks on Antibiotics
risks.summary: Growing regulatory restrictions on antibiotics in livestock (24% of revenue) threaten the company's operating results.
risks.score_rationale: Regulatory restrictions on livestock antibiotics affect 24% of revenue. EU ban 2022 on preventive antibiotics, Vietnam ban January 2026. Other bans possible. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Impact of Trade Tariffs
risks.summary: Changes in U.S. trade policy and retaliatory tariffs could increase costs and impact international operations.
risks.score_rationale: New U.S. tariffs imposed in 2025-2026 could affect imports. Material impact on 2025 results limited but future risk remains. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Bovaer Adoption Risks
risks.summary: The absence of government incentives is slowing Bovaer adoption, a key sustainability product, requiring continued investments to support its growth.
risks.score_rationale: Bovaer adoption has been slowed by the freeze in government incentives in 2025. Additional studies and expansion of indications may be needed to reach expected potential. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Restructuring Charges
risks.summary: Significant restructuring charges and site closures could disrupt operations in the short term, although $60M in savings are expected by 2027.
risks.score_rationale: $155M in charges in 2025, with an additional $25-30M expected in 2026. Site closures in Monheim and Kansas City planned for 2026. (default score, to be refined)
